verdict.rationale: Airbyte documents running pipelines locally. The OSS quickstart and abctl spin up a local Airbyte instance in Docker, and PyAirbyte extracts data into local caches, which suits notebook or prototype iteration without a server. However, no workflow is documented for testing a pipeline against a lightweight destination and then promoting it to production. A 2021 community report of a failed local docker-compose install predates abctl and lowers confidence rather than creating a dispute. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of a lightweight local destination (e.g., which cache backend), a documented local-to-production promotion or test workflow, independent hands-on corroboration of current local runs.

support.subject: As a data engineer, I run and test a pipeline locally against a lightweight destination before it touches production

citations.quote: This quickstart guides you through deploying a local instance of Airbyte Core, Airbyte's open source product.
abctl is Airbyte's open source command line tool to create and manage local instances of Airbyte running in Docker.
Data can be extracted from sources and loaded into caches
It's a good choice if you're using Jupyter Notebook or iterating on an early prototype for a large data project and don't need to run your own server.
